findings.summary: waitForStartedWorker calls readWorkerResult(runId)/hasRunExited(runId) without a channel argument, so the new blocking wait always polls the default RUNS_CHANNEL_ID even when runWrite was given a non-default opts.runsChannelId (used at tick-run.ts:1870/1875/1927). Latent only: no CLI flag populates runsChannelId today, so production always uses the default and the mismatch is unreachable; the pre-existing generate path at tick-run.ts:1689 has the same shape. If runsChannelId were ever wired, the wait would poll an empty channel and kill the tick with a misleading C5-fix2 timeout.

After a successful wait, runs[id] is force-set to {state:'exited', exitCode:0} for every card whose result arrived, overwriting a genuine non-zero agent.run.exited code present on the channel. A worker that publishes worker.result.v1 and then exits non-zero is now harvested to explored instead of reclaimed/retried by decideTick's exitCode branch (tick.ts:229-243). This is defensible and matches how the triage/generate poll paths already ignore exit code once a result exists, but it is a semantic change the spec does not explicitly call for.

coveredClueIds is computed from board and evidence channel reads at tick-run.ts:1886-1895, before the wait and harvest, but is passed to decideTermination at line 2208 after the harvest has published new evidence. The pass that actually harvests therefore reports coverage stale by one pass and increments zeroGrowthRounds. Not a spec violation (zeroGrowthThreshold is 2, so no premature convergence in that pass, and the next pass observes coverage > 0) and pre-existing rather than introduced by C5-fix2, but it makes that pass's termination.coverage understate what the tick just accomplished.
